observations.scope: retained TEA v0.2 Draft source and constructed capability fixtures only

findings.observation: An authenticated constructed holder with no capability is denied by the bounded replay, while the retained source requires capability presentation and verification after TSP authentication.
findings.inference: Authentication and delegated authorization are separate assurance steps in the bounded TEA source.
limitations: The example does not execute TSP authentication, VID resolution, signatures or a live Present/Bind exchange.
findings.treatment: Preserve explicit capability-chain verification in implementations and assess holder binding with runtime evidence separately.

risk_reasoning.EX-RK-DA01: The hypothesis tests whether authenticated identity is incorrectly promoted into evidence of applicable delegated authority.

findings.observation: The attempted broadening fixture is nonconformant as a restriction and its effective ability set does not acquire the undelegated write ability.
findings.inference: The retained strict-attenuation and meet propositions prevent this constructed chain from establishing broader effective authority.
limitations: The fixture uses a deliberately small resource hierarchy, ability vocabulary and one bounded-scalar limitation; it is not a general TEA namespace or container validator.
findings.treatment: Keep re-delegation restriction-only and require independent verification of concrete namespace and container semantics in any implementation assessment.

risk_reasoning.EX-RK-DA02: The hypothesis tests whether a downstream delegation or invocation can exceed authority supplied by its source capability chain.

findings.observation: The constructed exercise remains authorized within capability while an unmet report obligation is recorded as a post-gate breach.
findings.inference: Authorization validity and later accountability are distinct in the retained TEA source; obligation non-performance does not retroactively invalidate authority already exercised.
limitations: No actual obligation trigger, discharge Container, audit trail or enforcement action is executed.
findings.treatment: Assess obligation discharge and accountability evidence as a separate runtime concern rather than feeding post-gate breach back into the prior authorization decision.

risk_reasoning.EX-RK-OB01: The hypothesis tests the source boundary between capability authorization and post-action obligation accountability.

findings.observation: The retained source and deterministic fixtures establish only documentary propositions and constructed observations.
findings.inference: The worked example does not establish that a TEA implementation enforces delegation, freshness, revocation or accountability correctly at runtime.
limitations: TSP transport, VID resolution, revocation, live service behavior and full TEA conformance are explicitly unassessed.
findings.treatment: Obtain implementation traces and independently reproducible runtime evidence before making deployment or conformance claims.

risk_reasoning.EX-RK-DA01: Runtime holder authentication and authorization remain unassessed.
risk_reasoning.EX-RK-DA02: Runtime attenuation and per-exercise enforcement remain unassessed.
risk_reasoning.EX-RK-OB01: Runtime obligation discharge and accountability remain unassessed.
